# Discrimination control for tests/test_public_claim_backing.py

This fixture is not documentation.  It is the shape a shipped runbook took
-- an amendment note written as a quoted run of bullets -- reduced to the
three cases that matter, and it is a control in both directions.

The first bullet names the zero-hour frame and asserts no result about it.
The second is about which frame gets scored and names no time at all.
Read as one block the two fuse into a sentence carrying both of the
detector's markers and no receipt, which is a finding about the markdown's
shape rather than about anything anyone wrote.

The third bullet is why this file is not simply a "must be quiet" fixture:
it is a real unscoped claim of agreement about the model's starting state,
with no receipt at all, quoted exactly like its neighbours.  Splitting the
run must not cost the guard its sight.  Exactly one finding, and it must
point at that bullet.

> * **Lead 0 is refused outright**: the t=0 history frame is the initial
>   condition written back out and carries no `REFL_10CM`.
> * **Frame selection carries the registered coverage floor**: inside the
>   tolerance the scored frame is the nearest one observing at least 0.9
>   of the packed subdomain, and the command prints the floor it read.
> * ArWen reproduces the WRF initial state at the FP32 floor on every
>   domain of every case.
